source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Public Esther 1–6 binds the 105 matching original Hebrew records, including all source notes. Chapters 7–10 remain outside this draft batch.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Retain the identification formula and the full territorial span and province count without silently replacing the royal name with Xerxes.
verses.before: Now it happened in the days of Ahasuerus—the Ahasuerus who reigned from India to Cush, over one hundred twenty-seven provinces—
verses.after: This happened in the days of Ahasuerus, the Ahasuerus who ruled over 127 provinces, from India to Cush.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now it happened in the days of Ahasuerus—the Ahasuerus who reigned from India to Cush, over one hundred twenty-seven provinces—

verses.rationale: Distinguish the fortified royal center from the surrounding city while keeping the throne image.
verses.before: in those days, when King Ahasuerus sat on the throne of his kingdom in the citadel of Susa,
verses.after: In those days, King Ahasuerus ruled from his royal throne in the citadel of Susa.
verses.tsw_comparator: in those days, when King Ahasuerus sat on the throne of his kingdom in the citadel of Susa,

verses.rationale: Unfold the assembled groups in readable clauses; the military establishment remains distinct from provincial officials.
verses.before: in the third year of his reign, he gave a feast for all his officials and servants. The army of Persia and Media, the nobles, and the officials of the provinces were before him.
verses.after: In the third year of his reign, he held a banquet for all his officials and attendants. The army of Persia and Media, the nobles, and the provincial officials were there before him.
verses.tsw_comparator: in the third year of his reign, he gave a feast for all his officials and servants. The army of Persia and Media, the nobles, and the officials of the provinces were before him.

verses.rationale: Keep the extravagant duration and paired descriptions rather than reducing them to a generic royal celebration.
verses.before: He displayed the riches of his royal glory and the splendor and honor of his greatness for many days, one hundred eighty days.
verses.after: For 180 days he displayed the riches of his glorious kingdom and the splendor of his great majesty.
verses.tsw_comparator: He displayed the riches of his royal glory and the splendor and honor of his greatness for many days, one hundred eighty days.

verses.rationale: Distinguish the second banquet and its wider guests from the preceding display.
verses.before: When these days were completed, the king gave a feast lasting seven days for all the people who were present in the citadel of Susa, from the greatest to the least, in the courtyard of the garden of the king’s palace.
verses.after: When those days were over, the king held a seven-day banquet in the garden courtyard of the royal palace for everyone present in the citadel of Susa, from the greatest to the least.
verses.tsw_comparator: When these days were completed, the king gave a feast lasting seven days for all the people who were present in the citadel of Susa, from the greatest to the least, in the courtyard of the garden of the king’s palace.

verses.rationale: Render the sumptuous materials concretely, with a note qualifying the uncertain names of the paving materials.
verses.before: There were white and violet linen hangings fastened with cords of fine linen and purple to silver rings and marble pillars; couches of gold and silver were upon a pavement of porphyry, marble, mother-of-pearl, and dark stone.
verses.after: White cotton and blue-violet hangings were fastened with cords of fine linen and purple wool to silver rings and marble pillars. Gold and silver couches stood on a pavement of alabaster, marble, mother-of-pearl, and colored stone.
verses.tsw_comparator: There were white and violet linen hangings fastened with cords of fine linen and purple to silver rings and marble pillars; couches of gold and silver were upon a pavement of porphyry, marble, mother-of-pearl, and dark stone.

verses.rationale: Preserve differing vessels and royal abundance, recasting the idiom of the king's hand as provision.
verses.before: Drinks were served in vessels of gold, vessels differing from one another, and royal wine was abundant according to the king’s generosity.
verses.after: Drinks were served in gold vessels, each different from the next. The royal wine flowed freely, as generously as only a king could provide.
verses.tsw_comparator: Drinks were served in vessels of gold, vessels differing from one another, and royal wine was abundant according to the king’s generosity.

verses.rationale: Keep the explicit absence of compulsion in this particular rule, without extending it to the court's other practices.
verses.before: Drinking was according to the rule: “No compulsion.” For the king had instructed all the officials of his household to do according to each person’s desire.
verses.after: The rule for drinking was that no one was to be compelled. The king had instructed every official of his household to let each man do as he wished.
verses.tsw_comparator: Drinking was according to the rule: “No compulsion.” For the king had instructed all the officials of his household to do according to each person’s desire.

verses.rationale: Preserve the parallel banquet and separate group of guests.
verses.before: Queen Vashti also gave a feast for the women in the royal house that belonged to King Ahasuerus.
verses.after: Queen Vashti also held a banquet for the women in King Ahasuerus's royal palace.
verses.tsw_comparator: Queen Vashti also gave a feast for the women in the royal house that belonged to King Ahasuerus.

verses.rationale: Name all seven attendants and retain wine's effect without specifying an unstated degree of intoxication.
verses.before: On the seventh day, when the king’s heart was merry with wine, he commanded Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carkas, the seven eunuchs who served before King Ahasuerus,
verses.after: On the seventh day, when the king was cheerful with wine, he gave an order to Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcas—the seven eunuchs who attended King Ahasuerus.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the seventh day, when the king’s heart was merry with wine, he commanded Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carkas, the seven eunuchs who served before King Ahasuerus,

verses.rationale: Preserve the command and its objectifying purpose; do not add the unsupported claim that she was to appear naked.
verses.before: to bring Queen Vashti before the king wearing the royal crown, to show the peoples and the officials her beauty, for she was beautiful in appearance.
verses.after: They were to bring Queen Vashti before the king wearing her royal crown, to show the peoples and officials her beauty, for she was beautiful to look at.
verses.tsw_comparator: to bring Queen Vashti before the king wearing the royal crown, to show the peoples and the officials her beauty, for she was beautiful in appearance.

verses.rationale: State her refusal without inventing her motive; retain the burning image for his response.
verses.before: Yet Queen Vashti refused to come at the king’s command that was delivered by the eunuchs. Then the king became very angry, and his fury burned within him.
verses.after: But Queen Vashti refused to come at the king's command delivered by the eunuchs. The king became furious, and anger burned within him.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Queen Vashti refused to come at the king’s command that was delivered by the eunuchs. Then the king became very angry, and his fury burned within him.

verses.rationale: Keep the experts' description open rather than narrowing it to astrology or modern legal practice.
verses.before: Then the king said to the wise men who understood the times—for this was the king’s custom toward everyone who knew law and judgment,
verses.after: The king consulted the wise men who understood the times, for it was his practice to bring such matters before those who knew law and judgment.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king said to the wise men who understood the times—for this was the king’s custom toward all who knew law and judgment,

verses.rationale: Explain seeing the king's face as access while preserving all seven names and their rank.
verses.before: and nearest to him were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan, the seven officials of Persia and Media who saw the king’s face and sat first in the kingdom—
verses.after: Those closest to him were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan. These seven officials of Persia and Media had access to the king and held the highest rank in the kingdom.
verses.tsw_comparator: and nearest to him were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan, the seven officials of Persia and Media who saw the king’s face and sat first in the kingdom—

verses.rationale: Make the question's speaker clear and retain the royal third-person self-reference within his speech.
verses.before: “According to law, what is to be done to Queen Vashti because she did not carry out the command of King Ahasuerus delivered by the eunuchs?”
verses.after: “According to the law, what should be done to Queen Vashti?” he asked. “She has not carried out King Ahasuerus's command delivered by the eunuchs.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “According to law, what is to be done to Queen Vashti because she did not carry out the command of King Ahasuerus delivered by the eunuchs?”

verses.rationale: Keep the sweeping accusation explicitly in Memucan's voice rather than making it the narrator's judgment.
verses.before: Memucan said before the king and the officials, “Queen Vashti has not wronged the king alone, but also all the officials and all the peoples who are in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus.
verses.after: Memucan answered in the presence of the king and the officials, “Queen Vashti has wronged more than the king. She has wronged all the officials and all the peoples throughout King Ahasuerus's provinces.
verses.tsw_comparator: Memucan said before the king and the officials, “Queen Vashti has not wronged the king alone, but also all the officials and all the peoples who are in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus.

verses.rationale: Preserve the advisor's predicted chain of imitation and the quoted refusal.
verses.before: For the queen’s action will become known to all women, causing them to despise their husbands in their eyes when they say, ‘King Ahasuerus commanded Queen Vashti to be brought before him, but she did not come.’
verses.after: For the queen's conduct will become known to all the women, and they will look down on their husbands. They will say, ‘King Ahasuerus ordered Queen Vashti brought before him, but she did not come.’
verses.tsw_comparator: For the queen’s action will become known to all women, causing them to despise their husbands in their eyes when they say, ‘King Ahasuerus commanded Queen Vashti to be brought before him, but she did not come.’

verses.rationale: Retain the immediate alarm and emphatic sufficiency idiom without treating the prediction as established fact.
verses.before: This very day the noble women of Persia and Media who hear of the queen’s action will speak likewise to all the king’s officials, and there will be contempt and anger enough.
verses.after: This very day, the noblewomen of Persia and Media who have heard what the queen did will speak the same way to all the king's officials. There will be contempt and anger enough!
verses.tsw_comparator: This very day the noble women of Persia and Media who hear of the queen’s action will speak likewise to all the king’s officials, and there will be contempt and anger enough.

verses.rationale: Keep the proposed legal permanence, exclusion, and comparative judgment within the advisor's recommendation.
verses.before: If it is good to the king, let a royal decree go out from before him, and let it be written among the laws of Persia and Media so that it cannot be revoked: Vashti will no longer come before King Ahasuerus, and the king will give her royal position to another who is better than she.
verses.after: If it pleases the king, let him issue a royal decree, and let it be written into the laws of Persia and Media so that it cannot be revoked: Vashti must never again come before King Ahasuerus. Let the king give her royal position to another woman, someone better than she is.
verses.tsw_comparator: If it is good to the king, let a royal decree go out from before him, and let it be written among the laws of Persia and Media so that it cannot be revoked: Vashti shall no longer come before King Ahasuerus, and the king shall give her royal position to another who is better than she.

verses.rationale: Preserve the empire-wide promise of domestic obedience as the conclusion of the speech.
verses.before: When the decree that the king makes is heard throughout all his kingdom, though it is vast, all women will give honor to their husbands, from greatest to least.”
verses.after: When the king's decree is heard throughout his vast kingdom, all the women will honor their husbands, from the greatest to the least.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When the decree that the king makes is heard throughout all his kingdom, though it is vast, all women will give honor to their husbands, from greatest to least.”

verses.rationale: Keep approval and implementation distinct but concise.
verses.before: The word was good in the eyes of the king and the officials, and the king did according to the word of Memucan.
verses.after: The king and his officials liked this advice, and the king did as Memucan proposed.
verses.tsw_comparator: The word was good in the eyes of the king and the officials, and the king did according to the word of Memucan.

verses.rationale: Retain both script and language and the difficult final domestic-language clause; qualify its relation to the decree in a note.
verses.before: He sent letters to all the king’s provinces, to each province in its own script and to each people in its own language, that every man should be ruler in his own house and speak according to the language of his people.
verses.after: He sent letters to every royal province, to each province in its own script and to each people in its own language: every man was to rule his own household and speak the language of his own people.
verses.tsw_comparator: He sent letters to all the king’s provinces, to each province in its own script and to each people in its own language, that every man should be ruler in his own house and speak according to the language of his people.

verses.rationale: Avoid inventing regret or renewed affection where the source says remembered.
verses.before: After these things, when the anger of King Ahasuerus had subsided, he remembered Vashti, what she had done, and what had been decreed against her.
verses.after: Later, when King Ahasuerus's anger had subsided, he remembered Vashti, what she had done, and what had been decreed against her.
verses.tsw_comparator: After these things, when the anger of King Ahasuerus had subsided, he remembered Vashti, what she had done, and what had been decreed against her.

verses.rationale: Preserve the court's specified category and passive recruitment proposal without calling it a voluntary contest.
verses.before: Then the king’s young men who served him said, “Let beautiful young virgins be sought for the king.
verses.after: The king's young attendants said, “Let beautiful young virgins be sought for the king.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king’s young men who served him said, “Let beautiful young virgins be sought for the king.

verses.rationale: Make the imposed gathering and custody clear, using the recurring reading name Hegai consistently.
verses.before: Let the king appoint officers in all the provinces of his kingdom to gather every beautiful young virgin to the citadel of Susa, to the house of the women, into the hand of Hegai, the king’s eunuch who has charge of the women, and let their beauty treatments be given to them.
verses.after: Let the king appoint officers in every province of his kingdom to gather all the beautiful young virgins into the women's quarters in the citadel of Susa. Put them in the care of Hegai, the king's eunuch who guards the women, and give them beauty treatments.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let the king appoint officers in all the provinces of his kingdom to gather every beautiful young virgin to the citadel of Susa, to the house of the women, into the hand of Hegai, the king’s eunuch who has charge of the women, and let their beauty treatments be given to them.

verses.rationale: Retain royal pleasure as the stated criterion rather than recasting selection as achievement.
verses.before: Then let the young woman who is good in the king’s eyes become queen in place of Vashti.” The matter was good in the king’s eyes, and he did so.
verses.after: Then let the young woman who pleases the king become queen in Vashti's place.” The king liked the proposal and acted on it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then let the young woman who is good in the king’s eyes become queen in place of Vashti.” The matter was good in the king’s eyes, and he did so.

verses.rationale: Preserve the ancestry and leave the sentence connected to the following relative clause.
verses.before: There was a Judean man in the citadel of Susa whose name was Mordecai son of Jair, son of Shimei, son of Kish, a Benjaminite,
verses.after: There was a Jewish man in the citadel of Susa named Mordecai, son of Jair, son of Shimei, son of Kish, a Benjaminite,
verses.tsw_comparator: There was a Judean man in the citadel of Susa whose name was Mordecai son of Jair, son of Shimei, son of Kish, a Benjaminite,

verses.rationale: Keep the relative clause's consequential ambiguity about its antecedent; explain the issue in a note rather than choosing an unexpressed family subject.
verses.before: who had been carried into exile from Jerusalem with the exiles who were carried away with Jeconiah king of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried into exile.
verses.after: who had been taken into exile from Jerusalem with the captives deported with King Jeconiah of Judah, whom King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon had taken into exile.
verses.tsw_comparator: who had been carried into exile from Jerusalem with the exiles who were carried away with Jeconiah king of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried into exile.

verses.rationale: Clarify the guardian relationship while retaining both names, kinship, orphanhood, and the bodily description.
verses.before: He was bringing up Hadassah—that is, Esther—the daughter of his uncle, for she had neither father nor mother. The young woman was beautiful in form and appearance, and when her father and mother died, Mordecai took her as his own daughter.
verses.after: Mordecai was raising Hadassah, also called Esther, his uncle's daughter, because she had neither father nor mother. The young woman had a lovely figure and a beautiful face. When her parents died, Mordecai had taken her as his own daughter.
verses.tsw_comparator: He was bringing up Hadassah—that is, Esther—the daughter of his uncle, for she had neither father nor mother. The young woman was beautiful in form and appearance, and when her father and mother died, Mordecai took her as his own daughter.

verses.rationale: Preserve Esther's passive being taken and the repeated custody language; do not imply she volunteered.
verses.before: When the king’s command and decree were heard and many young women were gathered to the citadel of Susa into the hand of Hegai, Esther also was taken to the king’s house, into the hand of Hegai, keeper of the women.
verses.after: When the king's command and decree were announced, many young women were gathered into the citadel of Susa under Hegai's care. Esther too was taken to the king's palace and placed in the care of Hegai, the guardian of the women.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the king’s command and decree were heard and many young women were gathered to the citadel of Susa into the hand of Hegai, Esther also was taken to the king’s house, into the hand of Hegai, keeper of the women.

verses.rationale: Keep Hegai as the subject and distinguish provisions, seven attendants, and placement.
verses.before: The young woman was good in his eyes and gained favor before him. He quickly provided her beauty treatments and her portions, and seven chosen young women from the king’s house. He moved her and her young women to the best place in the house of the women.
verses.after: She pleased him and won his kindness. He quickly supplied her beauty treatments and special portions of food, assigned her seven selected attendants from the king's palace, and moved her and her attendants to the best place in the women's quarters.
verses.tsw_comparator: The young woman was good in his eyes and gained favor before him. He quickly provided her beauty treatments and her portions, and seven chosen young women from the king’s house. He moved her and her young women to the best place in the house of the women.

verses.rationale: Retain the two concealed affiliations and the stated source of the instruction.
verses.before: Esther had not revealed her people or her kindred, for Mordecai had commanded her not to make it known.
verses.after: Esther had not revealed her people or her family background, because Mordecai had instructed her not to tell.
verses.tsw_comparator: Esther had not made known her people or her kindred, for Mordecai had commanded her not to make it known.

verses.rationale: Preserve ongoing concern and the passive question about Esther's treatment.
verses.before: Every day Mordecai walked back and forth before the courtyard of the house of the women to learn Esther’s welfare and what was happening to her.
verses.after: Every day Mordecai walked back and forth in front of the courtyard of the women's quarters, trying to learn how Esther was and what was being done with her.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every day Mordecai walked back and forth before the courtyard of the house of the women to learn Esther’s welfare and what was happening to her.

verses.rationale: Keep the twelve-month total and the two six-month periods without compressing the regimen.
verses.before: When the turn came for each young woman to go in to King Ahasuerus, after she had been treated twelve months according to the regulation for women—for thus were the days of their beauty treatments completed: six months with oil of myrrh and six months with perfumes and women’s treatments—
verses.after: Each young woman's turn to go to King Ahasuerus came after twelve months under the prescribed treatment for women: six months with oil of myrrh and six months with perfumes and other beauty treatments.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the turn came for each young woman to go in to King Ahasuerus, after she had been treated twelve months according to the regulation for women—for thus were the days of their beauty treatments completed: six months with oil of myrrh and six months with perfumes and women’s treatments—

verses.rationale: Preserve the limited choice within the controlled process without implying broader freedom.
verses.before: then in this way the young woman went to the king: whatever she said was given to her to take with her from the house of the women to the king’s house.
verses.after: When a young woman went to the king, she was given whatever she asked to take with her from the women's quarters to the king's palace.
verses.tsw_comparator: then in this way the young woman went to the king: whatever she said was given to her to take with her from the house of the women to the king’s house.

verses.rationale: Retain the overnight sequence, transfer to concubine custody, and dependence on a personal summons.
verses.before: In the evening she went in, and in the morning she returned to the second house of the women, into the hand of Shaashgaz, the king’s eunuch who had charge of the concubines. She did not go in to the king again unless the king delighted in her and she was called by name.
verses.after: She went in the evening and returned in the morning to the second women's quarters, under the care of Shaashgaz, the king's eunuch who guarded the concubines. She would not go to the king again unless he delighted in her and summoned her by name.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the evening she went in, and in the morning she returned to the second house of the women, into the hand of Shaashgaz, the king’s eunuch who had charge of the concubines. She did not go in to the king again unless the king delighted in her and she was called by name.

verses.rationale: Keep the fuller parentage and adoption reminder while separating Hegai's advice from the broader response.
verses.before: When the turn came for Esther daughter of Abihail, the uncle of Mordecai who had taken her as his daughter, to go in to the king, she asked for nothing except what Hegai the king’s eunuch, keeper of the women, advised. Esther gained favor in the eyes of everyone who saw her.
verses.after: When the turn came for Esther—daughter of Abihail, the uncle of Mordecai, who had adopted her as his daughter—to go to the king, she asked for nothing beyond what Hegai, the king's eunuch and guardian of the women, advised. Esther won the favor of everyone who saw her.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the turn came for Esther daughter of Abihail, the uncle of Mordecai who had taken her as his daughter, to go in to the king, she asked for nothing except what Hegai the king’s eunuch, keeper of the women, advised. Esther gained favor in the eyes of everyone who saw her.

verses.rationale: Retain passive taking and all three dating details.
verses.before: Esther was taken to King Ahasuerus into his royal house in the tenth month, which is the month of Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign.
verses.after: Esther was taken to King Ahasuerus in his royal palace in the tenth month, the month of Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign.
verses.tsw_comparator: Esther was taken to King Ahasuerus into his royal house in the tenth month, which is the month of Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign.

verses.rationale: Preserve the paired comparisons and the crown's connection to Vashti's removal.
verses.before: The king loved Esther more than all the women, and she gained favor and steadfast kindness before him more than all the virgins. He set the royal crown on her head and made her queen in place of Vashti.
verses.after: The king loved Esther more than all the other women. She won his favor and affection more than all the other virgins, so he placed the royal crown on her head and made her queen in Vashti's place.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king loved Esther more than all the women, and she gained favor and steadfast kindness before him more than all the virgins. He set the royal crown on her head and made her queen in place of Vashti.

verses.rationale: Use the broader relief for an uncertain administrative benefit rather than specifying a tax remission or holiday as certain.
verses.before: Then the king gave a great feast for all his officials and servants, Esther’s feast. He granted relief to the provinces and gave gifts according to the king’s generosity.
verses.after: The king held a great banquet for all his officials and attendants—Esther's banquet. He granted relief to the provinces and gave gifts with royal generosity.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king gave a great feast for all his officials and servants, Esther’s feast. He granted relief to the provinces and gave gifts according to the king’s generosity.

verses.rationale: Keep the unexplained second gathering and gate location without supplying a reconstructed chronology.
verses.before: When virgins were gathered a second time, Mordecai was sitting at the king’s gate.
verses.after: When the virgins were gathered a second time, Mordecai was sitting at the king's gate.
verses.tsw_comparator: When virgins were gathered a second time, Mordecai was sitting at the king’s gate.

verses.rationale: Retain the reversed order of concealed affiliations and the continuing guardian relationship.
verses.before: Esther had still not revealed her kindred or her people, as Mordecai had commanded her, and Esther continued to carry out Mordecai’s word as she had when he was bringing her up.
verses.after: Esther still had not revealed her family background or her people, as Mordecai had instructed her. She continued to follow his instructions just as she had when he was raising her.
verses.tsw_comparator: Esther had still not made known her kindred or her people, as Mordecai had commanded her, and Esther continued to carry out Mordecai’s word as she had when he was bringing her up.

verses.rationale: Preserve the two names, guard role, and violent intent without adding a motive for their anger.
verses.before: In those days, while Mordecai was sitting at the king’s gate, Bigthan and Teresh, two of the king’s eunuchs from the guardians of the threshold, became angry and sought to lay hands on King Ahasuerus.
verses.after: In those days, while Mordecai was sitting at the king's gate, Bigthan and Teresh, two of the king's eunuchs who guarded the entrance, became angry and plotted to lay hands on King Ahasuerus.
verses.tsw_comparator: In those days, while Mordecai was sitting at the king’s gate, Bigthan and Teresh, two of the king’s eunuchs from the guardians of the threshold, became angry and sought to lay hands on King Ahasuerus.

verses.rationale: Make the information chain explicit and render in Mordecai's name as attribution.
verses.before: The matter became known to Mordecai, and he told Queen Esther. Esther told the king in Mordecai’s name.
verses.after: Mordecai learned of the plot and told Queen Esther. Esther then reported it to the king, giving Mordecai the credit.
verses.tsw_comparator: The matter became known to Mordecai, and he told Queen Esther. Esther told the king in Mordecai’s name.

verses.rationale: Preserve execution on wood without specifying rope hanging or impalement as certain; retain the written record that matters later.
verses.before: The matter was investigated and found to be so, and the two were hanged on a tree. It was written in the book of the chronicles before the king.
verses.after: The matter was investigated and found to be true. Both men were hung on a wooden stake, and the event was recorded in the book of the chronicles in the king's presence.
verses.tsw_comparator: The matter was investigated and found to be so, and the two were hanged on a tree. It was written in the book of the chronicles before the king.

verses.rationale: Retain the descent label and elevated seat rather than replacing the image entirely with a modern office title.
verses.before: After these things King Ahasuerus promoted Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite and exalted him. He set his seat above all the officials who were with him.
verses.after: After these events, King Ahasuerus promoted Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite. He raised him up and gave him a seat above all the other officials with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: After these things King Ahasuerus promoted Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite and exalted him. He set his seat above all the officials who were with him.

verses.rationale: Preserve the paired gestures and repeated refusal without adding a religious explanation absent from the narrative.
verses.before: All the king’s servants who were at the king’s gate bowed down and prostrated themselves before Haman, for so the king had commanded concerning him. But Mordecai would not bow down or prostrate himself.
verses.after: All the king's attendants at the king's gate bowed and knelt before Haman, as the king had commanded. But Mordecai would neither bow nor kneel.
